method: Evidence pack from the release file; one Sonnet 5.5 agent established the facts with exact quotes; every quote checked against the release files and README by script; the facts that set the level checked again by hand; level from the fixed rule; label and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
label: Downloads and runs Python and PDF tools the first time you ask about a figure
summary: The first time you ask about a figure, it downloads a 265–491 MB bundle of Python and the Poppler PDF tools from the original llm-for-zotero's GitHub release and runs it, without asking; the README doesn't mention it. What's there now is standard software: we checked the macOS (Apple silicon) bundle, and every file is from conda-forge.

facts.what: A 'PDF figure runtime' zip (Python 3.11, Poppler and scientific libraries), 265-491 MB depending on platform, from the original llm-for-zotero author's GitHub release, unpacked into a Zotero data folder; its Python then runs the plugin's pdf_figure_extract.py
facts.publisher: yilewang, the developer of the original llm-for-zotero
facts.notes: Not recorded as a fork in the pack, but it is the same code as the already reviewed llm-for-zotero--tcxm (UI Edition) and by the same owner TCXM/tcxm. Repo in pack: github.com/tcxm/llm-for-zotero-ui; the download address points at github.com/yilewang/llm-for-zotero, the original author's repository, so source is third-party. Code check: the managed-runtime block of content/scripts/llmforzotero.js (validateManagedRuntime through resolveManagedPdfFigureExtractionRuntime, about 290 lines from line 61658) is identical to the original-based qingyun0118 copy and to llm-for-zotero.json's description, apart from bundler renames of helper identifiers (pathExists5/6, ensureDir5 and the like). Requested runtime: PDF_FIGURE_RUNTIME_VERSION = "1" (tag pdf-figure-runtime-v1); same as original review. Path: figure extraction (the raw source-PDF figure extractor, which spawns the downloaded python with pdf_figure_extract.py) calls resolvePdfFigureExtractionRuntime() -> resolveManagedPdfFigureExtractionRuntime() -> installManagedRuntime() -> downloadRuntimePackageBytes(url) (fetch, then Zotero.HTTP fallback), then unzips with unzipSync, writes files, marks them executable and validates. If an installed runtime exists it is reused; the download happens only when none does. No confirmation dialog is involved (the confirm() calls in the bundle are for other features such as clearing the library index). Integrity: validateManagedRuntime only checks runtime.json kind/version/platform, that paths are inside the root and that the files exist; no hash compared, the SHA-256 digest calls elsewhere in the bundle are unrelated. Not checked: the zip contents (taken from the original review, same asset). Asset sizes via gh api on yilewang/llm-for-zotero tag pdf-figure-runtime-v1: macos-arm64 264976195 B, macos-x64 308167232, linux-x64 491361590, linux-arm64 336633041, windows-x64 and arm64 318226342 each. README: no mention of the figure runtime download (the word 'runtime' there refers to Codex App Server / Claude runtime). Original review (llm-for-zotero.json) called this developer-own because it is yilewang's own plugin; for a fork it is third-party, as in llm-for-zotero--tcxm.json.
facts.reviewerNote: Same runtime address and download code as llm-for-zotero (pdf-figure-runtime-v1 from yilewang/llm-for-zotero); contentChecked is from that review, of the same release file.

contentChecked: macOS Apple-silicon bundle (pdf-figure-runtime-v1, sha256 d2ea2815…): all 72 packages are from conda-forge and every file matches conda-forge's published hashes; the one extra file is a 22-byte anonymous usage token Anaconda's tools write. Other platforms not checked.
